newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish border town braces for new fight with river.
newsitem.headline: Polish border town braces for new fight with river.

text.p: The Polish town of Slubice on the German border fought to survive the swollen Oder River on Tuesday, bracing for another flood surge against sodden dikes in the next 24 hours.
Elsewhere in southwestern Poland, flood waters receded and weather forecasts were for more sunshine and only occasional showers, government crisis committee spokesman Krzysztof Pomes told Reuters.

Pomes said Slubice, across the river from Frankfurt an der Oder, could be flooded any time if its eroded dikes yielded to a river still about three metres (10 feet) above the alarm level despite having declined in the last two days.
"The easing of the water level is a very good sign but the dikes are soggy and water pressure is very high so they can still break at any moment," he said.
More than 16,000 people were evacuated from Slubice, situated in a low-lying area, and troops, police and firefighters continued frantic sand-bagging.
"The dikes have been strengthened by plastic sheets and sandbags but 90 percent of the citizens have been evacuated because the threat of flooding is very real," Pomes said.
The situation in Slubice, normally vibrant with cross-border trade, was aggravated by water receding from flooded zones on the German side of the river, increasing pressure on the dikes.
"If they break, the water which would flood Slubice may reach seven metres in some parts of town," Pomes said.
Some 2,000 residents stayed in Slubice at their own risk and food for them was sold from trucks because all shops, with entrances protected by sandbags, were closed.

Poland was hit by catastrophic floods more than three weeks ago. More than 6,000 square km were swamped and more than 150,000 were evacuated. Analysts estimate damages at up to 7.5 billion zlotys ($2.2 billion).
On Tuesday, almost 2,000 sq km were still under water and almost 40,000 people remained displaced.
Police revised the flood death toll downwards on Tuesday to 54 from 55, saying one of the dead was subsequently determined to have been murdered.
The government has began massive reconstruction of the affected areas and has said it will consider issuing bonds next year to help finance the rebuilding.
It has rejected the idea of a flood tax proposed by some opposition groups ahead of parliamentary elections on September 21.
Opposition parties have strongly criticised the ruling coalition of ex-communists (SLD) and peasants (PSL) for the way they handled the crisis.
The latest opinion polls showed the SLD-PSL team losing popularity as a result of the natural disaster.
